title: Network Monitoring Technologies

header.html: 3.2 Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies: methods (SNMP with traps, MIB, versions and community strings, flow data, packet capture, baseline metrics and anomaly alerting, log aggregation with syslog and SIEM, API integration, port mirroring); solutions (network discovery, traffic analysis, performance, availability and configuration monitoring)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1SNMP

Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) monitors and manages devices. A manager (NMS) talks to agents on devices.

Term Meaning
MIB (management information base) The database of values an agent exposes, each with an object identifier (OID)
Polling (GET) The manager asks for values (UDP 161)
Trap The agent sends an alert on its own when an event occurs (UDP 162)
v1 / v2c Community strings (like passwords) sent in clear text
v3 Authentication and encryption, user-based security: use this

Exam tip

. SNMPv3 is the secure version. Default community strings (public, private) must be changed or disabled.

2Other monitoring methods

Method What it gives
Flow data (NetFlow, IPFIX) Summaries of conversations: who talks to whom, how much, on which ports; traffic analysis
Packet capture Full packet contents for deep troubleshooting (Wireshark, tcpdump)
Baseline metrics Normal levels of utilization, latency, errors; deviations trigger anomaly alerting and notifications
Log aggregation Collect logs in one place: syslog collector; a SIEM (security information and event management) correlates events and alerts
API integration Tools pull data and trigger actions programmatically
Port mirroring (SPAN) The switch copies traffic from a port or VLAN to another port where an analyzer or IDS listens

3Monitoring solutions

Solution Meaning
Network discovery Finds devices, ad hoc (on demand) or scheduled
Traffic analysis Who uses the bandwidth (flow data)
Performance monitoring CPU, memory, bandwidth, latency, errors
Availability monitoring Is it up? (ping, service checks, uptime)
Configuration monitoring Detects changes against the baseline
Exam tip

. "See the full contents of traffic" = packet capture. "See who is using the bandwidth, with little data" = flow data. "Send a copy of traffic to an IDS" = port mirroring.

Exam tip

. Traps are sent by the agent; polls are asked by the manager; SNMPv3 is the secure version.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An administrator wants a switch to send an unsolicited alert when a link fails. Which SNMP feature fits?

  • AA GET poll
  • BA trap
  • CA community string
  • DA MIB walk
Show the answer

Answer: B. Traps are alerts sent by the agent.

S2A security team wants the most secure SNMP version with authentication and encryption. Which should be used?

  • ASNMPv2c
  • BSNMPv1
  • CSNMP with the default community string
  • DSNMPv3
Show the answer

Answer: D. SNMPv3 adds authentication and encryption.

S3An engineer needs to know which hosts consume the most bandwidth without capturing every packet. What fits?

  • APacket capture
  • BPort mirroring to a protocol analyzer
  • CFlow data
  • DSyslog only
Show the answer

Answer: C. Flow data summarizes conversations and volume.

S4An IDS must inspect a copy of all traffic from one switch port. What should be configured?

  • ALink aggregation
  • BPort mirroring
  • CA native VLAN
  • DSpanning tree
Show the answer

Answer: B. Port mirroring copies traffic to an analyzer.

S5A team wants logs from all devices stored centrally and correlated for security events. Which solution fits?

  • AA SIEM with syslog collection
  • BA patch panel
  • CA wireless heat map
  • DA DHCP relay
Show the answer

Answer: A. SIEMs aggregate and correlate logs.

S6Utilization suddenly doubles compared with normal. Which practice helps notice this?

  • AA golden configuration
  • BBaseline metrics with anomaly alerting
  • CAn asset inventory
  • DA cable map
Show the answer

Answer: B. Baselines make abnormal behavior visible.

4.2 Recall questions

R1Which ports does SNMP use?

Show the answer

UDP 161 for queries and 162 for traps.

R2What does a MIB contain?

Show the answer

The values (OIDs) an SNMP agent exposes.

R3What is the difference between SNMPv2c and v3?

Show the answer

v2c uses clear-text community strings; v3 adds authentication and encryption.

R4What is NetFlow an example of?

Show the answer

Flow data.

R5What does a SIEM do?

Show the answer

Aggregates and correlates logs and alerts on events.

R6What does port mirroring do?

Show the answer

Copies traffic from one port to another for analysis.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
SNMP manager and agent; MIB; GET (161); traps (162); v3 secure, v2c community strings
Methods flow data (summaries), packet capture (full), baselines, syslog + SIEM, API, port mirroring
Solutions discovery (ad hoc or scheduled), traffic, performance, availability, configuration monitoring
